name: Lakota and other Oceti Sakowin Nations
scope: Partner-selected Nations; no single collective study boundary
relationship: Existing ESIIL educational relationships are documented; participation in this proposed series is not confirmed.
evidence: ESIIL STARS includes Oglala Lakota College. Observing Unci Maka describes community-developed earth-observation methods.
question: Which relationships among grassland fire, grazing, drought and community priorities would participating Nations want to examine?
learn: Begin with the existing relationships and each Nation’s own definitions of useful evidence.
retain: Study areas, culturally important outcomes and release decisions remain specific to each participating Nation.

name: San Carlos Apache
scope: A separate potential case led by interested San Carlos Apache partners
relationship: San Carlos Apache College participates in STARS; this does not establish a Tribal government research agreement.
evidence: STARS publicly lists San Carlos Apache College student work on drought and, in an earlier cohort, air quality with Tohono O’odham Community College.
question: Could locally chosen fire–drought or smoke questions build on the existing student projects?
learn: Connect a new question to educational work that partners already find useful.
retain: College participation, Tribal government authority and community permissions are distinct.

name: Southern Ute Indian Tribe
relationship: A CU collaboration is publicly reported; participation in this new series is not confirmed.
evidence: Southern Ute describes forestry, fuels and prescribed fire services. Its newspaper reported a CU Boulder–USFS collaboration on treatment impacts and Tribal cultural values in the Brunot Area.
question: What monitoring or synthesis would complement the existing Brunot Area collaboration and the Tribe’s own forestry questions?
learn: Support existing work and distinguish cultural values from generic fuel-reduction metrics.
retain: Treaty-use and ancestral-land questions may extend beyond reservation boundaries; the relevant extent must be defined with the Tribe.

name: Ute Mountain Ute Tribe
relationship: No ESIIL partnership for this series is asserted.
evidence: The BIA Ute Mountain Ute Agency lists forestry and fire-management branches. This establishes an agency context, not the Tribe’s preferred research agenda.
question: Which woodland, fuels, resource-use or community-protection questions would the Tribe want a synthesis team to support?
learn: Ask the Tribe which existing programs and priorities should shape a case.
retain: Do not infer Tribal staffing, capacity, priorities or governance from the federal agency listing.

name: Yurok / Cultural Fire Management Council
scope: Separate organizational and Tribal authorities must be identified
relationship: Potential learning relationship; no invitation or agreement is implied.
evidence: CFMC is a community-based nonprofit whose stated mission connects cultural burning on the Yurok Reservation and ancestral lands with ecosystem health, protection, hunting and gathering.
question: What would practitioners choose to share about sustaining cultural fire, teaching, access and community-defined outcomes?
learn: Learn from practitioner-defined purposes and the institutional work that enables them.
retain: CFMC and Yurok Tribal government are not interchangeable authorities; public materials do not grant access to restricted knowledge.

name: Karuk Tribe
relationship: Potential learning relationship; no invitation or agreement is implied.
evidence: Karuk public materials describe cultural-fire practitioner support. Good Fire II addresses barriers to beneficial fire; a published California agreement offers an example of enabling conditions.
question: Which lessons about authority, practitioner support and sustained implementation might inform discussions elsewhere?
learn: Examine enabling institutions alongside ecological observations.
retain: Karuk practices and California-specific arrangements are not transferable prescriptions for other Nations or states.
